newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BOUQUET FOR FISCHER, BRICKBAT FOR HOWARD ON REPUBLIC

New South Wales Liberal leader, Peter Collins, has praised Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, for entering the republic debate, but says the Prime Minister risks political division and electoral backlash by failing to embrace the issue.
Mr Collins has told the National Young Liberals convention in Melbourne, John Howard must spell out a time frame for debate on the issue this year, to maintain public confidence.

Mr Collins says it's now time the Prime Minister tackled the issue. He says avoiding the issue, and not delivering on the promised People's Convention, without a strong alternative, will lead to criticism and ultimately political division.
SEARCH FOR DIVER MISSING IN BASS STRAIT

A search is underway for a missing diver in Bass Strait near Point Lonsdale. The woman was with a professional diving group and was exploring a submarine called K-2, two nautical miles south west of Point Lonsdale.
Police were notified when she failed to re-surface this morning. Water Police, Airwing Search and Rescue Squad and the Peninsula Rescue Service are all involved in the search.
RABBIT CALICI VIRUS CONFIRMED IN TASMANIA
Laboratory tests have confirmed that a disease affecting rabbits in northern Tasmania is the rabbit calici virus.

The disease was first noticed and reported in the Meander area about a week ago and announced by the State Government on Wednesday. The calici virus originally escaped accidentally from a South Australian research station, and there was to have been a planned release in Tasmania later this year.

However, the Primary Industry Minister Bill Bonde, says its arrived in Tasmania either through insects blown across Bass Strait, or by someone who illegally released an affected rabbit. The arrival of the disease, which kills rabbits in 30 hours by causing blood clots, has been welcomed by farmers.
BONDI MURDER ACCUSED ALLOWED TO LIVE WITH MOTHER
The man charged with the murder of a British tourist at Bondi in September has returned to court seeking changes to his strict bail conditions.
Twenty-three year old Aaron Martin made a successful application in the Supreme Court to allow him to live with his mother in western Sydney instead of with his sister.
Mr Martin's mother told the court her son attends Alcoholics Anonymous meetings up to six times a week, is a good kid and takes notice of her.
Mr Martin was granted bail with stringent conditions last year after being charged in connection with the bashing death of Brian Hagland at Bondi Beach.
Mr Martin, and another man charged with being an accessory, are due to face a committal hearing in April.
BULLIMORE'S RESCUE THE TALK OF THE TOWN IN ENGLAND
A cousin of British yachtsman, Tony Bullimore, says interest in his dramatic rescue in England rivalled that of the first landing on the moon.
Sid Stevens says the nation's media has described Australia's navy and airforce as marvellous, praising their determination to find Mr Bullimore over several days.
Mr Stevens says the rescue has overshadowed the news that British billionaire, Richard Branson, failed in his bid to fly around the world in a balloon.
He says people had been waiting and listening for news of the rescue, similar to the moon landing.
FISCHER SAYS YACHT RACING SHOULD BE MOVED FROM ANTARCTICA
Acting Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says won't buy into the debate about who should pay for ocean rescues, but thinks yacht racing should be moved from Antarctica.
Australia's Defence Forces yesterday successfully completed the rescue of two solo round the world competitors, Thierry Dubois and Tony Bullimore, following the earlier rescue of Rafael Dinelli.
Mr Fischer says Australia carried out its obligations magnificently.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
